Dots at 0.285 and 0.57 turns (26.0 s) and 0.46 and 0.92 turns (27.2 s) sit where the counters say. At 26.0 s the counters read 'turns: 0.28' against 'turns: 0.57': see L5.

findings.text: In 03_2 the input and output turn counters are rounded separately. At 26.0 s (f13243) they read 'turns: 0.28' and 'turns: 0.57', although the point of the picture is that the output turns exactly twice as fast (2 x 0.28 = 0.56). The dot positions agree with an exact input of about 0.285 turns. A viewer checking the doubling sees a mismatch while the counters run. Deriving the output readout from the displayed input value (or rounding the input down to a value whose double rounds the same way) would avoid it. The same separate-rounding pattern was raised as F1 in the earlier final03 review; it is still present in master 80244e88.
